items.title: Parsedown keeps rendering our users' Markdown safely while it moves to modern PHP

fields.summary: Applications that turn authors' and users' Markdown into HTML (P2), some of it untrusted (P4), get the same HTML from a strictly typed library on PHP 8.2 or later.

items.title: Pin down today's output before changing the code

fields.summary: Golden HTML for the fixtures, the options, and the security modes, and tests that run without the network.

items.title: Modernise the library in place with strict types

fields.summary: Strict types and typed signatures, public API first, extension API behind a compatibility layer, with byte-identical output.

items.title: Golden HTML of the current release

fields.summary: The HTML Parsedown 1.8.0 produces for the 64 fixtures, the public options, and hostile input in each mode, captured at a pinned commit.
fields.problem: Nothing but the fixtures says what the output must be, and the options and security modes have no fixtures of their own (E10).
fields.scope: In: G1 (64 fixtures), G2 (text, line, breaks, autolinking off), G3 (hostile input in default, escaped, and safe modes). Out: the CommonMark specification tests, handled in hermetic-commonmark.

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want today's HTML captured for every fixture, option, and security mode, so that each modernisation step is held to it.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: Parsedown.php at commit 4e433a8 on PHP 8.2 and the cases file for case sets G1, G2, and G3; expected: aayu survey --golden captures 71 cases with exit code 0 and a manifest naming the commit
2. [api-trace] state: the captured G1 outputs and test/data/*.html; expected: all 64 are byte-identical
fields.scenario: Run the capture once with the characterisation driver.
fields.environment: Linux, PHP 8.2 CLI with mbstring, the repository only

items.title: Run the CommonMark tests without the network

fields.summary: As the maintainer, I want the CommonMark tests to read a pinned copy of the specification, so that they pass or fail for the same reason every time.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: phpunit with the network disabled; expected: CommonMarkTestStrict and CommonMarkTestWeak run against the pinned specification file and report the same counts on two runs
2. [api-trace] state: case set G1; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference
fields.measure: network requests during the test run
fields.scenario: Run phpunit twice with outbound network blocked.

items.title: Strict types and a typed public API

fields.summary: declare(strict_types=1) and typed parameters and returns on text, line, parse, instance, and the five setters.
fields.problem: No public method declares a type (E15), so callers learn about wrong arguments only from wrong output.
fields.scope: In: the public methods and the version constant. Out: protected methods, which subclasses override (typed-extension-api).

items.title: Declare strict types and type the public methods

fields.summary: As a developer calling Parsedown, I want typed public methods under strict types, so that a wrong argument fails at the call instead of producing wrong HTML.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: the modernised Parsedown.php on PHP 8.2 and case sets G1, G2, and G3; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference in 71 cases
2. [api-trace] state: text(null) called from a file with strict types; expected: a TypeError naming text and its string parameter
fields.scenario: Replay the three case sets, then call text with null.

items.title: Typed extension API that existing subclasses still load with

fields.summary: Typed parameters on the protected block and inline methods, without return types that would break overriding subclasses (R1).
fields.problem: Extensions override protected methods found by name (E3, E8); adding return types would stop them loading.
fields.scope: In: parameter types on protected methods, the BlockTypes and InlineTypes tables unchanged. Out: return types on protected methods until Q1 says which subclasses exist.

items.title: Type the protected methods' parameters and keep subclasses loading

fields.summary: As a maintainer of a Parsedown extension, I want my subclass to keep loading and rendering the same HTML after the library is typed, so that I can upgrade without changes.
fields.completion_goal:
1. [api-trace] state: test/SampleExtensions.php unchanged, loaded with the modernised Parsedown; expected: both classes load and testRawHtml and testTrustDelegatedRawHtml pass
2. [api-trace] state: case sets G1, G2, and G3; expected: aayu survey --parity reports no difference
fields.measure: subclasses that fail to load; differences
fields.scenario: Run the extension tests, then replay the case sets.

items.title: The readme says PHP 7.1+ but composer requires 7.2

fields.summary: The readme and composer.json disagree on the oldest supported PHP version.
fields.reproduce: Read readme.md line 16 and composer.json line 16.
fields.expected: Both state the same minimum version.
fields.actual: The readme says Tested in PHP 7.1+; composer.json requires php >=7.2.
fields.completion_goal: 1. [api-trace] state: readme.md and composer.json after the fix; expected: both name the same minimum PHP version, and composer validate passes

open_questions: Q1 (open): which applications subclass Parsedown or use Parsedown Extra; decides whether protected methods may ever get return types
Q2 (open): byte-identical where Parsedown differs from CommonMark, or move towards it; no item changes output until answered
Q3 (open): whether callers rely on instance() sharing settings; no item touches instance() until answered
Q4 (open): the PHP floor; the items assume 8.2, the version characterised
